newsitem.title: USA: WMX says lays off several hundred workers.
newsitem.headline: WMX says lays off several hundred workers.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said it has laid off permanently "several hundred" U.S. mid-level managers and office support staffers at its Oak Brook, Ill., headquarters and nine other U.S. locations.
The company said the layoffs could continue. "At present, it probably effects several hundred people ... There could be more layoffs," said WMX spokesman Bill Plunkett.
He declined to specify the number of people who have lost their jobs, when the layoffs began or when they might end.
WMX employs 65,000 people, three-fourths of them in North America.
The layoffs started toward the end of 1996, continued into January and involved employees in WMX's Waste Management groups, said Plunkett later from a WMX board meeting in Florida.
Shares in WMX, the largest U.S. garbage hauler with $10 billion in annual revenues, were up 1/8 to 36-3/4.
The company is under intense pressure from large shareholders to make more money and has been selling off non-core and underperforming operations.
WMX is scheduled to report fourth-quarter financial results next week.
